title: WPSS/1284/2015 of Umesh Kumar Vs Indian Institute Of Technology Roorkee AND OTHERS

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Writ Petition (S/S) No. 1284 of 2015

Versus
Indian Institute of Technology, Roorkee & others
 Ö.ÖRespondents
Honíble Sudhanshu Dhulia, J.
1. Mr. Bilal Ahmed, Advocate, present for the
petitioner.
2. Mr. Rajendra Singh Azad, Advocate, present
for the respondent No.4.
3. Mr. Vipul Sharma, Advocate, present for the
respondent Nos.1 to 3.
4. This writ petition was dismissed for non-prosecution on 15.09.2016.
5. Learned counsel for the petitioner has moved
Delay Condonation application (CLMA No.11688 of 2016)
along with Restoration application (MCC No. 767 of 2016)
and has prayed that delay in filing restoration application
may be condoned.
6. Grounds shown in the affidavit are sufficient
and bona fide to condone the delay in filing the restoration
application. The delay condonation application is allowed.
Delay is condoned. Heard on the Restoration application
No.767 of 2016.
7. The restoration application is allowed on the
grounds urged. Order dated 15.09.2016 passed by this
Court is hereby recalled. The writ petition is restored to its
original number.
8. The petitioner is working as an Assistant
Library Information Officer (in short ìALIOî) in Indian
Institute of Technology, Roorkee. On a complaint moved by

2
respondent No.4, who is represented by Mr. Rajendra Singh
Azad, an allegation has been made against the petitioner
that the father of the petitioner was in Government Service
of Union of India and after his retirement his mother is
dependent upon his father, yet the petitioner has shown
his mother to be dependent upon him and is taking
monetary benefits for it. Consequently, two orders have
been passed. One is order dated 16.12.2014, by which the
hospital booklet of his mother was asked to get
surrendered and another is order dated 29.12.2014, by
which inquiry has been ordered.
9. Since the matter is presently being enquired
into, it will not be proper for this Court to interfere in the
matter.
10. The writ petition stands dismissed. However,
the respondents are directed to expedite the inquiry. It is
further made clear that the dismissal of the present writ
petition will not prejudice the inquiry in any manner.
